transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is... my eating has just gotten so off lately. Some days I barely get down a cup of coffee and a granola bar before my shift. I work at the hospital, support staff, you know? And it's just been so busy. Like Tuesday, they had me running between three different floors because someone called out sick. People call out sick all the time now, especially since the new supervisor started. She's really strict about clocking in on the exact minute, which is ridiculous because the scanner at the main entrance is broken half the time. You have to swipe your badge like four times just to get it to beep, and it always holds up the line. 

But yeah, I don't know, I've just noticed my scrubs have been hanging really loose on me lately. I'm not trying to lose weight or anything, but they're just bagging off me now.
Have you noticed any significant weight loss recently, or have you been worried about gaining weight even though you're eating less?

Well, no, I'm definitely not worried about gaining weight. It's really the opposite, like I said, I'm just not eating. Some days it's literally just that coffee and a granola bar before my shift. And I know I've lost weight because of how loose my scrubs are getting. They used to fit perfectly, you know? I bought this one set online, not from the hospital uniform store because their prices are a total ripoff, but from this medical supply website my sister told me about. She used to be a dental hygienist before she moved to Florida. Anyway, the scrubs were great, really comfortable material, but now they're just bagging off me. I'm not trying to lose weight at all, it's just happening because my appetite is completely gone. I just don't have the energy to care about food right now.
Have you noticed any other physical changes or symptoms related to not eating enough, like feeling dizzy, weak, or cold more often?

Well, I don't know about dizzy or cold, really. But the weakness... yeah. I mean, it's this heavy, dragging feeling. Even after I've been in bed all night, trying to sleep, my body just feels like I just finished a double shift. And they do ask us to work doubles sometimes, especially on the weekends. The weekend shift differential is supposed to be good, but honestly, after taxes, it barely makes a dent. I used to pick up extra shifts all the time when I was trying to pay off my car. It's a Honda Civic, great gas mileage, which is important because my commute is like forty-five minutes now since they closed the highway exit near my apartment for construction. They said it would take six months to fix the bridge, but it's been over a year. 

But anyway, yeah, the tiredness is just constant. By lunchtime, I'm just... fighting to keep my thoughts together. It's like walking through mud. I just sit in the breakroom and stare at the wall. The breakroom microwave has been broken for two weeks, by the way. Someone tried to heat up fish in it and ruined the whole thing. It smells terrible. But I don't even care because I'm too exhausted to eat anyway.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I guess I have. I mean, I used to do a lot of stuff. I used to go running in Van Cortlandt Park all the time. It's a great park, really huge, but you have to be careful on some of the trails because the roots stick up and you can easily twist an ankle. My buddy Dave twisted his ankle there last summer and he was out of work for three weeks. He works in construction, so he really couldn't be on it. He actually had to fight with his union rep to get his full sick pay, which is just crazy because he pays his dues every month. 

But yeah, I used to run, and I'd take my camera out, take photos... I even used to play chess with some friends on the weekends. But lately, I just... I don't know. I look at my running shoes or think about calling the guys for a game, and I just tell myself there's no point. It just feels like too much effort for nothing. So I mostly just end up sitting at home, scrolling on my phone for hours, or just staring at my budget spreadsheet. I've been trying to track every penny because groceries are just getting so expensive. I went to buy eggs yesterday and they were almost six dollars a dozen. Six dollars! And they weren't even the organic ones, just regular eggs. It's getting to the point where you have to take out a loan just to make an omelet. But yeah, I just... I don't really care about doing any of the fun stuff anymore.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, like running or taking photos?

Yeah, like I was just saying, it's exactly that. The running in Van Cortlandt, the photography, the chess games with my friends... I just look at my camera or my running shoes and tell myself there's absolutely no point anymore. It's too much effort. So I just end up sitting at home on the couch, scrolling on my phone for hours or staring at that budget spreadsheet I mentioned. 

I use Excel for the spreadsheet, actually, but I had to track down an older CD-ROM version to install because Microsoft wants everyone to pay a monthly subscription now for Office 365. It's a total scam. Why would I pay every single month just to type numbers into a grid? My buddy Dave—the one who hurt his ankle—he tried to get me to use Google Sheets since it's free, but I really don't trust having my personal financial stuff floating around up in the cloud, you know? Hackers are getting into everything these days. Did you see on the news they hacked that big hospital system downtown last month? They had to divert all the ambulances to our ER, which made my shift an absolute nightmare. We were running out of stretchers in the hallway. 

But anyway... yeah. I just sit there looking at my expenses or staring at my phone. The interest in all the fun stuff is just completely gone.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past couple of weeks?

Yeah, it's pretty much every day. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge. My badge actually stopped scanning last week, by the way. I had to go all the way down to security in the basement to get it fixed, and the guy down there—he's this older guy, always wearing these thick glasses—he was trying to tell me I must have left it near a magnet. I don't even own any magnets! Well, except for the ones on my fridge, but those are just little plastic ones from the pizza place down the street. Luigi's Pizza. They make a really good white pie, but they stopped delivering to my building after 8 PM because the delivery guy's bike got stolen outside my lobby. Can you believe that? You can't even leave a bike for five minutes anymore. 

But yeah... that heavy feeling. It's just there all the time. I put on my scrubs and I just feel completely weighed down by it, all day long.
Have you noticed that your thinking has slowed down or that it's harder to concentrate on tasks, like following a conversation or making decisions?

Yeah, I guess... maybe? I don't know if my thinking is slowed down, exactly, but it is harder to concentrate on things. Like, I was trying to read this memo they sent out at work about the new hand hygiene protocols. They keep changing the protocols, I swear, every six months it's something new. They want us using this new foam sanitizer that smells like cheap perfume, and it totally dries out your hands. My knuckles are cracking from it. I actually had to go to the pharmacy to buy that heavy-duty working hands cream, the one in the green tub. It's supposed to be for construction workers, like my buddy Dave, but it works okay. The pharmacist there, she's always trying to push the store brand on me, saying it's the exact same ingredients, but I read the back and it's not. The store brand has some kind of alcohol in it, which is just going to dry my hands out even more. It makes no sense to put alcohol in a moisturizing cream, right? 

But anyway, yeah, I was trying to read that memo and I just... I couldn't get through it. I kept reading the same paragraph over and over, and none of it was sticking. So I guess, yeah, following along with things is definitely harder right now.
Would you say that your mood has been persistently low or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two weeks or more?

Two weeks? No, it's been way longer than two weeks. That steady, low feeling—the depression and just losing interest in everything—that settled in a bit later, but it’s been with me for roughly the past year and four months now. 

I know exactly how long it's been because it started right around the time they decided to repave the employee parking garage at work. They shut down three whole levels with zero warning, just put up these orange cones one morning. We all had to park in this dirt overflow lot across the street, right next to this old diner. Not a Denny's, but one of those greasy 24-hour places. The seagulls hang out by their dumpsters all day, and I swear, if you parked anywhere near the fence, your car just got absolutely covered in bird mess. I had to take my Honda to the car wash on Route 9 like twice a week. And that car wash used to be five bucks, but now they charge twelve, and they don't even towel dry it anymore. You just drive through this giant blower and it leaves hard water spots all over the windshield. It drives me crazy when the sun hits the glass and you just see all those little spots, you know? You try to use the wiper fluid to clear it, but it just smears it around and makes it worse. I need to buy new wiper blades, actually, but they lock them behind plastic cases at the auto parts store now. You have to press a button to get an employee to unlock it, and you end up standing there for twenty minutes just waiting for someone to show up with a key. 

But yeah... anyway. It's been about a year and four months of feeling this way.
Have you experienced a significant change in your appetite or weight nearly every day for at least two weeks in a row?

Yeah, definitely. Actually, that's a big part of what brings me in, to be honest. My eating has gotten so off lately. Some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift, and that's it for the whole day. And my scrubs have been hanging loose on me, like I'm swimming in them, even though I'm not trying to lose weight or anything. 

Speaking of those scrubs, though, they just switched our supplier at the hospital. We used to have these nice, soft cotton blend ones, but now they're using this weird synthetic material that feels like wearing a plastic bag. They say it's more stain-resistant, which I guess is fine if you're spilling stuff all day, but they don't breathe at all. I was sweating through mine just walking from the parking lot last Tuesday. And the pants! The pockets are totally different. The old ones had that deep cargo pocket on the right side where I'd keep my penlight and my shears, but the new ones just have these shallow little slash pockets. My penlight fell out twice while I was helping transfer a patient. I had to order a special clip for it online, but the shipping was delayed because of that big storm up the coast. The tracking app kept saying "Out for Delivery," but it took three extra days. I hate when they do that. You just sit around waiting for the mail carrier, and our mail carrier, he's always listening to podcasts on his phone without headphones, just walking up the street blasting some true crime show. 

But yeah... I'm definitely losing weight without trying, and my appetite is just shot.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a major depressive episode with a recurrent course and moderate severity (F33.1). The patient endorses persistent low mood, loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities, significant weight loss and appetite disturbance, fatigue or loss of energy, and impaired concentration, all occurring nearly every day for more than two weeks.
